findings.what: The lesson never says why a motoring set must be tripped. The brief promised the reasons: unburned fuel in a motored diesel risks fire and explosion, and the healthy set carries the extra draw and can be overloaded. Screen 4 has room for one or two sentences (71 words); add them there and in the explain text.

findings.where: Screen 3 (B carries the rest), set up by screen 2's text
findings.what: Screen 2's words and its still say 'B carries 450.4 kW' one screen earlier, so the typed answer (450.4 kW) is a memory check rather than the sum. Give screen 3 its own numbers, for example a 360 kW share with a 40 kW draw, or drop the B figure from screen 2's text.

findings.where: Screen 9 (The first current), set up by screen 8's opening frame
findings.what: Screen 8's demonstration opens at 0 s with Current 5511 A and 6.67 times rated, and its line under the picture says 'The current is 5511 A, 6.67 times rated' (film s7, first frame). Screen 9 then draws the whole PMG curve with its dot at that peak. So screen 9's typed answer is on screen before Check. Start screen 8 after the first peak, or ask screen 9 with a different sub-transient reactance, and hide the curve on screen 9 until Check.

findings.where: Screen 7 (Where it slips), reachable from screen 6's slider
findings.what: On screen 6 the Time slider snaps to 1.2 s, and just past it the line under the picture reads 'E is below 0.48, so no angle can carry the 200 kW'. That puts screen 7's answer one drag away. Word that line without the figure, for example 'E is now too small for any angle to carry the 200 kW'.

findings.where: Screen 6 text and explain, lost field
findings.what: The step from 'no angle can carry the kW' to 'the rotor slips a pole' is skipped. Add one sentence: the engine still pushes 200 kW in, the set can no longer pass it out, so the extra power speeds the rotor past the board's field.

'A now draws 150 kVAr from the board' is given with no reason on screen; the explain text has it. A short sentence such as 'A weak field cannot send kVAr out, so A draws it in' makes the point land (about 87 words in all).
'Past 90°, no angle can carry the kW' reads as if δ goes beyond 90° and only then fails. Say 'Once E falls below 0.48, even 90° cannot carry the kW.'

The text gives A's power as 0.32 per unit, but the angles shown come from 200 ÷ 630 = 0.317. By hand with 0.32, sin δ = 0.48 ÷ 0.80 = 0.6 gives 36.9°, and 0.48 ÷ 1.44 gives 19.5°. Use 0.32 in the model, or quote 0.317.

'The middle period sits near 826.7 ÷ 0.25 = 3307 A' is loose. On the drawn curve the transient period starts near 3307 A and falls to about 2640 A by 0.5 s, so say 'starts near'. Also add 'per unit' to 'The transient reactance is 0.25'. Tie the division to the rule he already knows from transformers: fault current = rated current × 100 ÷ the percentage impedance.
The Timer tile reads 1.1 s at 2 s while the relay and its timer bar stay hidden until screen 4, so the reading has nothing to explain it. Hide the Timer tile on screen 2, as the bar is hidden.
'What do you change?' asks him to change protection settings, while the practice box says only authorised people set protection. Ask 'Which change stops this trip but still catches a stopped engine?'

The PMG case uses the settled 2480 A at the breaker's 0.5 s, then tells him to read the current at the trip time off the decrement curve. The curve gives 2636 A at 0.5 s. Use 2636 A, or say 'at least 2480 A'.

There are five footnotes, all on descriptive claims and none on a figure he would look up on a job, and [^4] and [^5] sit on neighbouring sentences. Keep one or two, such as the decrement curve and the shunt-fed decay, and drop the rest.
'In the set's own drawing, a short at its terminals leaves only Xs' is vague. Say 'In the simple model, E behind Xs, a short at the terminals leaves only Xs to hold the current back.'

findings.where: Lesson as a whole versus the brief
findings.what: The brief promised under- and over-voltage and frequency protection named on one screen. They appear only as a line in the practice box. One sentence on screen 12 or a short line in the explain would keep the promise.
